title: Man. Post. Cap. IX: PLAC — Adam's sin by imputation is neither committed by us nor inherent in us
pass_a_gloss: Placeus states the target claim: Adam's sin 'ours by imputation' (or immediately imputed) is, as to us, neither our deed nor inherent in us. Garrigues wants Adam's actual sin imputed, not inesse or done by us once born.
pass_b_english: That Adam's sin belongs to us by imputation—or, if you prefer, is proximately and immediately imputed to us—is, as far as we are concerned in the thing itself, neither committed by us nor inherent in us. The matter is plain about Adam's actual sin: for you want that imputed to us, not to be in us, or to be committed by us once born.
source_text: Quod Adami peccatum nobis per imputationem convenit, vel, si ita mavis, nobis proxime & immediate imputatur, id ex quo sumus reipsa neque a nobis commissum est, neque nobis inhaeret. Res manifesta est de peccato actuali Adami: id enim vis nobis imputari, non autem inesse, aut a nobis natis committi.

choices.choice: Imputed Adam-sin neither our act nor inherent
